steps.text: Combine the salt, sage and black pepper in a small bowl and rub on both sides of the chops. Melt the butter or margarine in a large skillet over medium high heat and saute the chops for 5 minutes per side, or until well browned.

Meanwhile, in a separate small saucepan over high heat, combine the water and the bouillon and stir until bouillon dissolves. Add this to the chops, reduce heat to low, cover and simmer chops for 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Sage Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: Pork chops rubbed with a pungent seasoning of dried sage, salt and pepper are pan fried in butter until golden brown then simmered in a simple beef bouillon.
raw_recipe.name: Sage Pork Chops

recipeInstructions.text: Combine the salt, sage and black pepper in a small bowl and rub on both sides of the chops. Melt the butter or margarine in a large skillet over medium high heat and saute the chops for 5 minutes per side, or until well browned.

Meanwhile, in a separate small saucepan over high heat, combine the water and the bouillon and stir until bouillon dissolves. Add this to the chops, reduce heat to low, cover and simmer chops for 45 minutes.

review.reviewBody: I used boneless pork chops and omitted the salt and these turned out perfect! They were very juicy and flavorful and they were plenty enough salty from the bouillon alone (I think they would have been much too salty with the extra 2 tsp. salt). At the end of cooking time I removed the chops from the pan and thickened the juices with 3 tablespoons cornstarch mixed with 3 tablespoons cold water and it made a nice, thick, brown gravy that had a very good flavor. I served the chops and gravy with mashed potatoes and broccoli spears. This was a delicious, easy meal that I would definitely make again!

My husband really enjoyed these! I used 4 bone-in center cut pork chops and omitted the salt as others suggested. I followed the rest of the recipe to the letter. When the chops were finished cooking, I removed them from the pan and mixed 1/4 cup of water with 1 tbsp. of corn starch and added it to the beef broth in the pan. I brought it to a boil and cooked it for 1 minute. It made a delicious gravy.

I leave out the sage and use ground white pepper instead of black pepper.
I also use half the butter and only use enough water to barely cover the chops completly. I simmer them on low for about an hour and 15 min. I have been cooking them like this for over 35 yrs and everybody just loves them this way. Another option is to add a can or two of cream of mushroom soup but use less water.

This recipe was a real hit with the family. Browned the pork chops for three minutes per side and cooked for 20 minutes. I added a dash of salt to the rub along with the sage and pepper. I also added a couple of pinches of garlic and onion powder. I used two cups of chicken broth as I wanted more gravy. I used 3 tbsp of corn starch mixed with the broth from the pan. I served it with garlic mashed potatoes also from this website. Next time I will leave the dash of salt out as it was just a tad too salty.

These were really tasty. I used olive oil instead of butter for a healthier fat and omitted the salt. When the pork chops were finished cooking, I removed them from the liquid and added in a couple of tablespoons of corn starch. I let it simmer for a few minutes until thickened for a yummy sauce and served it all over a bed of rice.

Good meal! I changed a few things. I omitted the salt after reading reviews (didn't miss it). I browned the pork chops for 1 minute each side. Used 2 teaspoons of bouillon granules in 1 cup of warm water and then I only cooked covered on low heat for about 25 minutes. Was very good with a surprisingly good flavor and stayed tender! I will make this one again.

Used 6 thick chops, 1T sage, no salt, 4 bouillon, 3 c. water, added 3 cloves of garlic and a chopped yellow onion. Used pam and sprinkled buttered flavoring over chops too. Simmered for 45min covered. Made gravy with 2T cornstarch. Served the chops with the gravy poured all over baked potatoes and broccoli too. OMG this was delish.

Very good. Glad I read the reviews and skipped the salt. It was perfect with the bouilion. I browned the chops the night before and put them in the frig. In the morning I put everything in the crockpot on low for 8 hrs, used the broth for gravy. Family loved it with mashed potatoes and broccoli.

My husband and I made this last night and we enjoyed it. We did take other reviewers' advice and thickened the beef gravy after pork was done cooking. We used 3 tablespoons corn starch to 3 tablespoons cold water. It thickened up after no time and was much needed. NOTE: The gravy is VERY salty since recipe calls for using 2 cubes to one cup water--double what you normally would--but it works well when you mix it with chops, mashed potatoes, etc. So, no worries there!

We also halved the salt content in rub, though could actually use more to help out the chop's flavor.

What we will try next time: Adding more sage per chop (I know one reviewer recommended 1 tsp PER chop), cooking for less time, and perhaps adding some garlic. Overall, it was a great, easy recipe that we will definitely make again.

Awesome! I took everyone's advice & didn't add any extra salt. After I sautéed the pork chops, I took them out & sautéed some minced garlic & thinly sliced shallot, then replaced the chops & added the beef broth. When it was done, I removed the chops & used cornstarch to make a gravy. Served with mashed potatoes. SO good!! Thanks for sharing!

I LOVED this recipe. I didn't realize it called for bone-in chops, and I only had boneless ones, but I just reduced the cooking time to about 30 minutes and they were succulent and delicious. I do agree with the comments about not adding any salt - the bouillon is salty enough on its own. I think I'm going to try this with chicken breasts too.

Such a wonderfully flavourful recipe that will be my new "go-to" pork chop recipe. I did not read the comments beforehand because I prefer to let my natural instinct govern. I also used a lesser cut of pork to try the recipe. I also used less salt in the rub, used fresh sage, and used a pork bouillon cube instead of beef. I cooked for the 45 minute required braising time and will reduce it next time. I served it with Italian-style roasted potatoes and an Irish butter cabbage recipe. YUM!

Very good quick recipe. Watch your cooking time on these chops. If the chops are less than 3/4 thick, you do not need 45 minutes. I cooked mine on the stovetop in less than 10 minutes to perfection. Otherwise, you will dry them out like most people because they fear undercooking pork. The meat keeps cooking after you take it out of the pan. I had fresh sage, fresh garlic clove, and a small fresh piece of rosemary. The flavor was excellent, but it needs a little something else to put it over the top.

I used a cheap, thinner, “low quality” bone in chop that i got on sale. 😬 This recipe and result? Was if I spent more!?!! It was great! Simple yet delicious! This cooking method and ingredients can make a tire taste good! So glad I tried! PS; save yourself a pot and just microwave the water and beef bouillon cubes. Would and will make again! Thank you Tiffany Nixon!
Definite Hit !
Loved it! I only had beef stock, but it all works well together. The recipe is great as it is.

I made this for the first time for my hubby who raves about the pork chops at a local diner. OMG...he went on and on about how wonderful these were and said they were so much better than those of the diner! They only change I made was cutting the salt by half (per other reviews) but increasing the amount of the total spice rub by a half. FANTASTIC recipe...THANK YOU!!

These were really good! The only change I made was using beef stock paste instead of beef bouillon cubes. My pork chops came out a little dry and salty, so I think I will reduce the cooking time and add less salt to the spice mixture next time. Aside from that, they had good flavor and were tender so I'll give it another go with those slight adjustments.
I've made this several times and my husband loves it. The pork is so tender! I thicker the broth to make a gravy towards 5he and and serve with mashed potatoes and veggies.
Yay this was a hit with the hubby! I doubled all the seasonings (I had very big chops) and I added 2 tbsp lemon pepper and about a half cup of parmesan cheese! Delicious!
